assessment: The incumbent supplies the intended course set in 32/40 exports, below the 95% target; overall median handling is 17 minutes. Unchanged-assignment centers achieve seven minutes, suggesting useful existing behavior, without establishing causality. Six affected exports coincide with assignment changes. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation: missing records and failed name matching remain distinguishable possibilities. Fast execution and slow replacements suggest delivery delay, but waiting is not necessarily handling. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish safety for the unsampled split-course center.

openings.claim: Current-assignment selection may omit courses for historical weeks; separately, renaming may make present courses appear absent during coordinator comparison.
openings.delta: Distinguish incorrect membership from recognition errors before changing export selection or labels.
openings.prediction: With an agreed intended set held fixed, assignment changes alter exported membership if the first mechanism holds; renaming preserves membership but disrupts coordinator matching if the second holds.
openings.probe: In private staging, compare fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split courses for one requested week. Compare internal course identities and exported rows with coordinator-agreed expectations; include another center as an isolation check. Retain the documented CSV schema and concurrent attendance entry. Time-box diagnosis within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Staging can reproduce assignment and naming transitions.
Agreement on intended courses can be established independently of current export output.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling arise mainly from reconciling course expectations, or from downloading and spreadsheet import?
openings.delta: Separates an unobserved workflow bottleneck from execution and replacement waiting time.
openings.prediction: If reconciliation dominates, active checking and correction expand on disputed-course files while download/import times remain similar; an import bottleneck produces a different allocation.
openings.probe: Use six coordinators’ two short sessions with fabricated ordinary and disputed-course CSVs, counterbalancing order. Time checking, correction, download and import separately; record passive waiting separately. Run within the same six-day budget using authorized workspaces without interrupting attendance entry.
assumptions: Fabricated files approximate ordinary spreadsheet workflows.
Session results guide a bounded change; they do not establish the next-40-export success measures.
